authorization_quote: Can we add an illustration for the article?
scope: Add symbolic editorial illustration alongside existing original photographs; preserve article prose and photo locations.
medium: Built-in ImageGen; watercolor and ink, symbolic not documentary
prompt: Create a wide 3:2 editorial illustration for a personal essay, 'A Week in Bhubaneswar: Conversations and New Beginnings'. Poetic Natural mode: spare pen-and-ink with translucent watercolor on warm ivory paper, human-drawn selective detail, muted indigo and earthy rust, generous quiet space. A slightly open old poetry notebook in the foreground, its written lines only tiny abstract marks, a simple pen beside it. One loose ink line from the page becomes a flowing thread, suggesting music and a journey, leading towards a small, lightly sketched contemporary café conversation in the middle distance: three ordinary adult Indian people in everyday clothes, seen obliquely, relaxed unequal poses, no recognizable portraits. A modest folded piece of plain woven cotton rests on the table, connecting writing and craft without claiming a particular textile tradition. Keep one coherent composition, avoid a collage of icons or a checklist of landmarks. The notebook is the emotional anchor; the people softly suggested, not detailed. A feeling of rediscovery, curiosity and quiet possibility. No literal musical notes, no temples, no ceremonial costumes, no readable words, no title, no logo, no border, no watermark. Clearly an illustration rather than a photograph or record of an actual meeting.
source_constraints: No real-person likeness, factual meeting reconstruction or claims of specific traditional cloth/landmarks.
coordination: Preserve Dhaga evidence integration and all existing publication receipts; no social publication or programme credit.
review: Root inspected generated image: clearly painterly notebook and conceptual thread/cafe/cloth; no legible invented verse or recognizable real people; generic city backdrop not an identified landmark.
